title: Seat a graphics card in a keyed x16 slot, square to 2 degrees so its bracket and far end go in with the edge connector
keywords: square insertion of a long part
instruction: Install the graphics card in the green riser board: put its gold edge connector into the black slot and its steel bracket into the gap at the slot's near end, and press the card straight down until it is fully seated.
context: Lenovo ThinkSystem SR645 V3 User Guide, Install a GPU adapter: "Align the GPU adapter with the PCIe slot on the riser card. Then, carefully press the GPU adapter straight into the slot until it is securely seated." https://pubs.lenovo.com/sr645-v3/install_a_gpu Done by: data-center technicians. A card left part way in is not detected or does not work (Lenovo ST50 troubleshooting, PCIe adapter not recognized: "The device is seated correctly", https://pubs.lenovo.com/st50/optional_device_problems).
setup: The two arm bases stand 61 cm apart on an oak table. A fixed green riser board, 277 x 80 mm and 6 mm thick, lies flat 9 to 17 cm right of the midline, its long side running out from the bases from 17 to 44.5 cm. On it, a black x16 slot (2.0 mm wide, keyed) runs from 22 to 30.5 cm out, with a steel bracket gap (2.9 mm) at its near end, 17.5 cm out, and a steel support channel (36 mm wide, its top 59 mm above the board, flared) at the far end, 38 to 43 cm out. A dual-slot graphics card (254 mm long, 111 mm tall, 35 mm thick, 350 g) with a steel end bracket stands on its gold edge connector in a blue foam stand 30.5 cm right of the midline, parallel to the riser, 18 to 43 cm out, bracket toward the bases.
scoring: Offsets are of the card from its seated place. Seated: within 1 mm of the seated height, 1.5 mm along the slot and 1.0 mm across it, tilted and turned under 2 degrees. 1.0 when seated and still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s) for 1 s, which ends the trial. Otherwise the last step scores 0.8 if seated but not still; 0.5 when the gold fingers are started into the slot (over the slot as for 0.2, under 8 mm above seated, within 1.5 mm along and across) but not seated; 0.2 when the card is over the slot with its bracket toward the bases (turned under 3 degrees, tilted under 5, within 3 mm along and across, at most 40 mm above seated), so its far end is in the support channel. Otherwise 0; a card turned end for end scores 0. The scorer does not see the grippers, so a card held seated counts the same as one let go.
reset_notes: Lift the card out of the slot and stand it back in the foam stand, bracket toward the bases.
fidelity: The card and riser are rigid bodies at full size; card height, length and finger sections are published PCIe sizes, the 35 mm thickness, bracket and riser are our estimates. The connector has no contacts or springs: a 1.6 mm board goes into a 2.0 mm slot with no insertion force. The slot's lead-in and the channel's flare are wider than real. No flex; at 350 g likely lighter than a real card. Friction 1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic on every object.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (2,400 steps; the card stays in its foam stand); demo: 1.0 (success at step 473)
